questions.stem: 提示：為了減少垃圾，有些學校規定學生餐廳不再提供免洗餐具，學生必須自備碗筷或餐盒才能取餐。請比較下列兩張圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一與圖二中學生餐廳在規定實施前後的不同；第二段說明你對這項規定的看法，並以你自己的經驗說明理由。

1.explanation_zh: 第一段是前後比較，兩張圖都要寫，並寫出「改變了什麼」；第二段要先說你贊成或反對，再用你自己的經驗說明理由。經驗可以是自備餐具的麻煩、忘記帶的糗事，或垃圾量的變化；只寫「保護環境很重要」不算經驗。
evidence: 第一段比較圖一與圖二中學生餐廳在規定實施前後的不同
並以你自己的經驗說明理由
1.strategy_zh: 比較段可抓三組對比：垃圾桶、學生手上的餐具、門口的設備；第二段可以用「一開始不方便 → 後來習慣 → 看到改變」的時間順序。
hints: 第一段：每組對比都要寫到圖一和圖二
第二段：立場一句，經驗依時間順序寫三四句
可以承認規定的不便，再說明為什麼仍然值得

moves.zh: 比較圖一與圖二中學生餐廳在規定實施前後的不同
說明你對這項規定的看法

content.focus_zh: 第一段要寫出規定前後至少兩組對比（垃圾桶滿出來 vs. 幾乎空了、拿免洗餐具 vs. 自備餐盒與洗手台）；第二段要有明確立場，並用自己帶餐具或用免洗餐具的具體經驗說明理由，可兼顧不便之處。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段以「規定前…；規定後…」對照；第二段先表態，再依時間寫經驗（一開始、後來、現在），最後回扣規定的意義。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在式與現在完成式（has been replaced by），經驗用過去式、現在的改變用現在式；not only … but also 前後要平行。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 餐具與垃圾相關的字（chopsticks、lunch box、single-use、trash can、waste、rinse）要用對，避免一直重複 trash 與 good for the environment。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

outline.closing_zh: 一條規定讓餐廳變得乾淨許多。

outline.topic_sentence_zh: 表明你對禁用免洗餐具的看法。

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show the school cafeteria before and after a new rule. In the first picture, a large trash can at the entrance is so full that its lid cannot close. Plastic spoons, paper cups, and chopsticks are lying on the floor around it. Several flies are circling above them. In the second picture, however, a sign on the wall says that the cafeteria no longer provides single-use bowls or chopsticks. Students are waiting in line with their own lunch boxes, and a few of them are washing their bowls at the sinks. As a result, the big trash can has been replaced by a small one that is almost empty.
I strongly support this rule because it really reduces waste. When I was in junior high school, I used single-use chopsticks and paper bowls every day without thinking. However, after my high school started the same rule last year, I began to carry a steel lunch box and a pair of chopsticks in my bag. At first, it was a little troublesome, since I had to wash them after every meal. For example, one day I forgot my chopsticks and had to borrow a spoon from my teacher. Now bringing my own tableware has become a habit, and our class produces much less trash than before. In conclusion, this rule not only protects the environment but also teaches students to take responsibility for their own waste.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
The two pictures tell a before-and-after story of a school cafeteria. In the first picture, taken before the new rule, the trash can at the entrance is overflowing: its lid cannot close, and plastic spoons, foam bowls, and paper cups have spilled onto the floor, attracting a few flies. A student stands nearby with an empty lunch box in his hand, unsure where to throw it away. The second picture shows the same room after the rule took effect, and it looks calmer and cleaner. A sign on the wall announces that disposable tableware is no longer provided, so students line up with their own steel containers and chopsticks while the cafeteria staff fill the containers with rice and vegetables. Instead of a mountain of garbage, the entrance now has a row of sinks, where several students are rinsing their bowls, and a small trash can that remains almost empty.
I fully support the ban, and my own experience shows why. Before my school introduced the same rule last year, I used at least two sets of disposable chopsticks and a paper bowl every day, which added up to roughly four hundred sets in a single school year. I had never thought about that number until our homeroom teacher asked us to count. When the ban began, I complained along with everyone else. Carrying a steel lunch box made my backpack heavier, and washing it in a crowded line after lunch felt like a waste of break time. For example, on one rainy day I forgot my chopsticks and had to eat fried rice with a borrowed spoon, much to my classmates’ amusement. Within a month, though, the routine became automatic, and the change was visible: the cleaning team on our floor now takes out one bag of trash a day instead of three. Admittedly, the rule can be inconvenient for students who buy lunch at the last minute, so the cafeteria could sell low-cost reusable sets. Still, the inconvenience is temporary, while the habit lasts. In the end, a rule that seemed strict at first has taught me that protecting the environment begins with what we carry in our own bags.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 比較段把前後差異寫得具體，經驗有數字、有轉折、有班上垃圾量的變化，讓步後還提出解決辦法與見解（內容 5）；依時間推進、轉承自然（組織 5）；分詞構句、非限定子句、much to one’s amusement 等句型正確（文法句構 5）；用字精確（overflowing、rinsing、inconvenient），仍以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段對照垃圾桶滿出、免洗餐具散落與蒼蠅 vs. 告示、自備餐盒排隊、洗手台與小垃圾桶；第二段先表態支持，依國中、去年開始、現在的時間順序寫自己的經驗，結尾 not only…but also 平行正確。無語言錯誤；As a result 接在洗餐具之後略牽強，For example （忘了帶筷子）與前一句「要洗餐具很麻煩」對應不夠緊，字彙平實。

top.comment_zh: 第一段以 before-and-after story 總括，細節（保麗龍碗、蒼蠅、拿著便當盒不知往哪丟的學生、洗手台、幾乎空的小垃圾桶）完整；第二段表態後依時間寫經驗（一年四百雙筷子的計算、一開始抱怨、忘了筷子用湯匙吃炒飯、一個月後養成習慣、垃圾從三袋變一袋），再讓步提出低價餐具組的配套，最後回扣規定的意義。句型與字彙（disposable tableware、rinsing、took effect）精準，無語言錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段用 In the first picture … In the second picture, however … 對照垃圾桶塞滿、蒼蠅與自備餐盒、洗手台、小垃圾桶，至少寫出兩組對比；第二段立場明確，依時間寫國中的習慣、規定實施後一開始的不便（忘了帶筷子）到現在的習慣，並以 not only … but also 回扣。文法與拼字都正確，句型與字彙正確但不特別突出。

top.comment_zh: 第一段以 before-and-after story 開場，把規定前後的垃圾桶、標語、排隊、洗手台與小垃圾桶完整對照；第二段用「一年約四百副免洗餐具」的數字、抱怨到習慣的過程、忘記筷子的趣事、清潔組垃圾由三袋變一袋，並讓步（臨時買午餐的學生）後回扣環保。句型與字彙豐富，時態轉換自然，沒有錯誤。
